author: wifi_content
acceptedClaims: WPA2-Personal passphrase and SSID derive PSK used as PMK; passphrase is not the literal 256-bit key.
PTK is derived for the pair; GTK is distributed by the AP.
PMKID is an identifier, not a separate frame; a suitable WPA2-Personal capture can support offline guessing.
Correct SAE provides passive offline-guessing resistance and forward secrecy; WPA2 Transition connections do not inherit SAE properties.
SAE anti-clogging is computational exhaustion mitigation, not a substitute for password attempt rate limiting.
6 GHz availability depends on regulatory domain; Enhanced Open provides encryption without peer authentication.
1/6/11 is a common channel plan, not the sole plan worldwide; corporate 40 MHz use has no universal prohibition.
SNR alone does not guarantee a QAM/MCS value; 802.11k reduces discovery work and 802.11r does not guarantee a fixed roam duration.
The 14 added glossary definitions have technically appropriate expansions and relevant lesson targets.
reviewerAuthoredCorrectionsRequiringAnot: RADIUS certificate renewal need not change CA; account/certificate revocation does not necessarily terminate existing sessions immediately.
PMF protects robust management frames after key establishment, not every frame or radio jamming.
Useful throughput has no universal fixed percentage of PHY rate.
DHCP troubleshooting includes VLAN, relay, server, filtering and local versus controller switching.
DFS CAC and post-radar Non-Occupancy Period are distinct; CAC does not replace the typical minimum 30-minute prohibition.

criteria.technical: Changed claims and new definitions independently read against IEEE RSNA/DFS terminology and cited RFC 7664/8110. Reviewer-authored corrections still need root review.
criteria.beginner: Changed claims explain password/key distinction, practical WPA3 limits and regulatory context. Whole-lesson terminology dispositions remain incomplete.
criteria.answerConsistency: No question keys or answer options changed. Full question-bank answer correctness was not reviewed by this reviewer.
criteria.lessonRelevance: All 14 new glossary targets match their Wi-Fi security or radio-planning topic. Exact browser navigation requires separate test evidence.
criteria.terminology: New definitions accepted in scope; no claim that every raw candidate in both full lessons has been independently dispositioned.
